note: South Africa, read on the Department of Home Affairs' own pages on 2026-10-30. A performer on a short engagement works on a visitor's visa with section 11(2) authorisation (the work engine's route). To live there, the General Work Visa is valid for the employment contract's length, at most 5 years, on an employment contract, so tied to the employer; an application inside the Republic is made in person no less than 60 days before the current visa expires, and missions abroad take applications too ('either'). Its published turnaround is 4 weeks, counted in working days. A holder of a work visa for five years with an offer of permanent employment may apply for direct permanent residence (section 26(a)), with a published turnaround of 8 months. Fees are set annually and paid at the office, not given on these pages, so none is written. The critical skills visa and permit (27(b)), the business visa and naturalisation's count aren't written.

sources.title: Department of Home Affairs, Types of Visas
sources.said: General work visas are valid for the duration of the contract of employment or a period not exceeding 5 years. ... The application is being submitted in person, no less than 60 days before the expiry date of the applicant’s visa ... Remember that there is a fee charged for issuing a visa, and you should check the cost with the office as well, as this is updated annually.

sources.title: Department of Home Affairs, Permanent Residency
sources.said: has been the holder of a work visa for five years and has proven to the satisfaction of the Director-General that he or she has received an offer for permanent employment.

sources.title: Department of Home Affairs, Turnaround times for visas and permits
sources.said: The listed turnaround times are not ordinary calendar days and must be calculated using working days only ... General Work Visa - Section 19(2) incl. TES 4 weeks ... Worker - Section 26(a) 8 months
